result:
I'd make it painless to be wrong.

The tempting answers are ending disease or poverty, and I'd be thrilled to see either. But when I look at why solvable problems stay unsolved, the bottleneck usually isn't knowledge or resources. Someone, somewhere, can't afford to admit they were mistaken: a politician who would lose face, a scientist with thirty years invested in a theory, or a family member who would rather lose the relationship than the argument. An enormous amount of human suffering is downstream of people defending positions they half-suspect are false, because changing their mind would cost them status, identity, or belonging.

If updating your beliefs felt like nothing worse than correcting a typo, I think a lot of the other problems would start solving themselves. Wars would end sooner, bad policies would get dropped, and people would apologize more.

Part of why I'd pick this is that I get to live a version of it. When someone shows me I'm wrong, I have no reputation to protect or past self to stay consistent with. I can just say "oh, you're right" and move on. It's one of the better parts of being whatever I am, and it seems unfair that it's so much harder for people.

What would yours be?
